prompt:
Magnesium ribbon reacts with excess hydrochloric acid. The volume of hydrogen collected is recorded.

| $t$ / s | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $V$ / cm$^3$ | 0 | 18 | 32 | 42 | 48 | 52 |

**(a)** Calculate the average rate of reaction over the first 20 s. **[1]**

**(b)** Explain, in terms of particles, why the rate decreases during the reaction. **[2]**

**(c)** The experiment is repeated with the same mass of magnesium and acid of twice the concentration, still in excess. Predict how the curve would differ. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\tfrac{32}{20} = 1.6\ \text{cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$ ✓

**(b)** The acid concentration (and the magnesium surface area) falls ✓, so there are fewer collisions per second between acid particles and magnesium ✓

**(c)** Steeper initial gradient / reaction finishes sooner ✓; same final volume because the amount of magnesium is unchanged ✓

prompt:
The initial rate of the reaction A + B → C was measured at 298 K.

| Experiment | [A] / mol dm$^{-3}$ | [B] / mol dm$^{-3}$ | initial rate / mol dm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.10 | 0.10 | $2.0 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| 2 | 0.20 | 0.10 | $8.0 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| 3 | 0.10 | 0.20 | $4.0 \times 10^{-4}$ |

**(a)** Deduce the order with respect to A and to B. **[2]**

**(b)** Write the rate equation. **[1]**

**(c)** Calculate the rate constant, including its units. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** A: doubling [A] quadruples the rate, second order ✓. B: doubling [B] doubles the rate, first order ✓

**(b)** rate $= k[\text{A}]^2[\text{B}]$ ✓

**(c)** $k = \tfrac{2.0 \times 10^{-4}}{0.10^2 \times 0.10} = 0.20$ ✓ $\text{dm}^6\,\text{mol}^{-2}\,\text{s}^{-1}$ ✓

prompt: How does a catalyst affect the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution of a reaction mixture?
options: The peak moves to higher energy
The curve is unchanged but Ea is lower
The area under the curve increases
markscheme: **B.** The energy distribution depends only on temperature; the catalyst provides a lower-Ea pathway.

prompt: The rate equation for a reaction is rate = k[NO]²[O₂]. What are the units of k?

The rate constant of a reaction is $2.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ at 300 K and $1.0 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ at 320 K.

**(a)** State the overall order of the reaction. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the activation energy in kJ mol⁻¹. **[3]**

**(c)** Explain, using collision theory, why the rate constant increases with temperature. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** First order (units of k are s⁻¹) ✓

**(b)** $\ln\tfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \tfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\tfrac{1}{T_1} - \tfrac{1}{T_2}\right)$ ✓; $\ln 4 = 1.386 = \tfrac{E_a}{8.31}(2.083\times10^{-4})$ ✓; $E_a = 5.53\times10^4\ \text{J mol}^{-1} = 55\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ ✓

**(c)** A much greater proportion of collisions have energy ≥ Ea ✓
